lesson: xcodebuild -only-testing:<Target>/<Suite>/<testName> exits 0 even when the identifier matches NOTHING (e.g. Swift Testing free functions whose identifier spelling differs) — it 'succeeds' having executed zero tests. Never accept a targeted re-run as a pass without confirming the test actually ran (grep the log for the named test case or a nonzero executed count). Also: piping xcodebuild/just through `grep|tail` swallows the exit status unless `set -o pipefail` or a separate `echo exit=$?` capture is used — capture the exit code explicitly for evidence.

topic: Homebrew zig upgrades silently break the pinned-version build
lesson: The target pins minimum/maximum Zig 0.15.x (build.zig.zon minimum_zig_version 0.15.2, requireZig fails on 0.16). Homebrew's plain `zig` formula auto-upgraded to 0.16.0, so the PATH default broke `zig build` with a comptime version error. The working toolchain remains installed as the keg-only formula zig@0.15: prefix PATH with /opt/homebrew/opt/zig@0.15/bin (zig 0.15.2) before running `zig build` / `just test`. Also: `echo $?` after `cmd | tail` reports tail's status — capture the build exit code with `cmd > log 2>&1; echo $?` instead.

Swift Testing's #expect macro cannot wrap a call to a mutating method on a local var ('cannot use mutating member on immutable value: $0 is immutable' — the macro closes over the value immutably). Write `let applied = state.mutatingCall(...)` first and then `#expect(applied)`. The error only surfaces at test-target compile time, so a test file can look fine until xcodebuild runs.
